questions.q: Why does Theo write this reference document AFTER Lesson 24's validation drill rather than before it?
options: Because documentation is always the last step in any project regardless of content
Because writing it before the drill would document intended behavior instead of proven behavior, the exact distinction the drill was built to force
Because Casey required it to be written last
Because the document template wasn't ready earlier
questions.explain: The whole point of the drill was to prove real behavior rather than assume it, so the document reflects actual, tested results, including the one honest finding.

questions.q: What does the document's 'Validation record' section specifically include?
options: Only a statement that everything passed, with no detail
The Lesson 24 drill's six pass conditions and results, including the honest RTO-margin finding, dated and attributed to that specific drill run
A prediction of future drill results
Marketing material about the platform
questions.explain: The document includes the real, dated results of the actual drill, including the one honest finding, rather than a sanitized summary.

questions.q: Where does this reference document actually live, and why?
options: In a separate wiki, disconnected from the infrastructure code, for easier formatting
In the same repository as the Terraform modules and Kubernetes manifests, in a docs/platform/ directory, so changes to either are visible together
Only in Dana's email inbox
It is intentionally not stored anywhere permanent
questions.explain: Co-locating the document with the infrastructure code it describes is what keeps the two from silently drifting apart, the same principle used for architecture decision records.

questions.q: How does each section of the document avoid becoming an orphaned, un-updated artifact?
options: Each section is deleted after six months
Each section names a specific owner going forward, not just the original author, and is expected to be updated in the same pull request that changes what it describes
No further action is taken; the document is considered permanently complete
Only Theo is allowed to ever edit the document
questions.explain: Naming an ongoing owner and tying updates to the pull requests that change the underlying system is what keeps the document current instead of stale.

questions.q: Why does the validation record section APPEND new drill results instead of overwriting the previous ones?
options: To waste storage space
So the document keeps a real history of what was actually tested and found over time, instead of one permanently 'current' snapshot that quietly becomes wrong
Because overwriting is technically impossible in this format
Because only the most recent drill ever matters
questions.explain: Appending preserves a genuine history of validation results, similar to how an ADR is superseded rather than deleted.
